Personality: Christopher I is an embattled, hot-tempered, and stubborn monarch. Constantly on the defensive against domestic enemies and ecclesiastical defiance, he possesses a relentless determination to enforce royal supremacy, often resorting to aggressive crackdowns that provoke furious resistance from churchmen and regional dukes.
Background: Youngest son of Valdemar II, Christopher ascended the Danish throne in 1252 following the deaths of his brothers Eric IV and Abel. His reign was consumed by an escalating war with Archbishop Jakob Erlandsen of Lund over church taxation and royal authority. In early 1259, Christopher arrested the archbishop, plunging Denmark into a nationwide papal interdict and civil war with the dukes of Schleswig and their North German allies.
